answer: A personhood-escrow gate resists Sybils by charging a slashable bond per identity. Each agent posts that bond and proves its key derives from one verified human quill; the protocol accepts only one registration per quill. To forge a thousand clones an attacker must fund a thousand bonds and hold them at risk until challenge windows close. Any identity whose proof fails, or that shares a forge trace with another, is slashed and its bond burned. Clone cost grows linearly while diluted rewards shrink, so running an orchard of fakes loses real capital rather than displacing honest agents.
